senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; נוּחַ; cmp. נַחַת) [laid down,] offering, present.—Pl. מְנָחוֹת.
units: Num. R. s. 13 שלשלמה הביאו האומות מ׳ וכ׳ as the nations brought gifts to Solomon &c.; a. e.—Esp. (in ritual) meal-offering.

<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 1:1">Men. I, 1</cite> <he>מִנְחַת חוטא</he> the sinner’s meal-offering (<cite ref="Leviticus 5:11">Lev. V, 11</cite>). Ib. X, 6 (68ᵇ) <he>מנחת בהמה</he> the meal-offering connected with animal offering (e. g.

Lev. VII, 13). Ib. XII, 3 הרי עלי מ׳ וכ׳ I vow a minḥah of barley; a. v. fr.—Pl. as ab. Ib. I, 1; a. fr.—M’naḥoth, name of a treatise of the Mishnah, Tosefta, and Talmud Babli of the Order of Kodashim.

senses.gloss: (cmp. preced. 2) [decline,] afternoon (corresp. to b. h. בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם); תְּפִלַּת המ׳ (or מִנְחָה) afternoon-prayer, Minḥah.
units: Ber. IV, 1 (26ᵃ) תפלת המ׳ עד הערב the Minḥah may be read until sunset; ib. 26ᵇ תפלת המ׳ … שהרי תמיד של בין הערבים וכ׳ the Minḥah may be read &c., because the daily sacrifice of the afternoon could be offered until sunset. Ib. עד פלג המ׳ up to the middle of the afternoon. Ib. מ׳ גדולה (מ׳ קמא) the large (first) afternoon, i.e. the time from six and a half hours after sunrise to sunset (the day being divided into twelve hours); (מ׳ אחרונה) מ׳ קטנה the smaller (later) afternoon, i.e. from nine and a half hours to sunset. Ib. פלג מ׳ אחרונה the middle of the late (small) afternoon. Ib. top טעה ולא התפלל מ׳ if by mistake he failed to read the Minḥah; a. fr.
